SHA-256 init, update, finalize, one-shot hash, and repeated 32-byte hash functions.

# Purpose
This C file implements the SHA-256 hash algorithm and the object life-cycle functions for the `fd_sha256_t` state object. It defines the required alignment and memory footprint through [`fd_sha256_align`](<#fd_sha256_align>) and [`fd_sha256_footprint`](<#fd_sha256_footprint>), then provides [`fd_sha256_new`](<#fd_sha256_new>), [`fd_sha256_join`](<#fd_sha256_join>), [`fd_sha256_leave`](<#fd_sha256_leave>), and [`fd_sha256_delete`](<#fd_sha256_delete>) to create, validate, detach, and destroy a SHA-256 state in shared memory. These functions check for `NULL` pointers, alignment, and the `FD_SHA256_MAGIC` value before use, and they clear or set the magic value with memory fences to control state visibility.

The file also contains the SHA-256 compression and digest routines. [`fd_sha256_init`](<#fd_sha256_init>) sets the initial hash state, [`fd_sha256_append`](<#fd_sha256_append>) adds input data in blocks while keeping partial data in an internal buffer, and [`fd_sha256_fini`](<#fd_sha256_fini>) applies SHA-256 padding and writes the final 32-byte digest. [`fd_sha256_hash`](<#fd_sha256_hash>) provides a one-shot hash interface, and [`fd_sha256_hash_32_repeated`](<#fd_sha256_hash_32_repeated>) hashes the same 32-byte message many times. The core block transform is selected at compile time: [`fd_sha256_core_ref`](<#fd_sha256_core_ref>) is a portable reference implementation, and [`fd_sha256_core_shaext`](<#fd_sha256_core_shaext>) uses Intel SHA-NI and SIMD instructions when `FD_HAS_SHANI` is enabled.
